evidence: Three clearly identified gaps with thorough literature analysis (research/01_landscape_analysis.md)
Each gap maps to a specific architectural innovation with falsification condition
Gap 1 (MRF-DW): No prior ConvNeXt variant uses within-block multi-scale depthwise mixing
Gap 2 (LE-GRN): No prior work adds local mean removal to GRN in ConvNeXt blocks
Gap 3 (Adaptive Expansion): No principled study of stage-specific expansion for ConvNeXt at <20M
concerns: All three innovations are engineering improvements rather than fundamental architectural breakthroughs
MRF-DW shares conceptual similarity with MixConv (channel-split multi-scale DW convs)
The combination of three small innovations may produce a model that is better than any one individually, but attributing gains to specific components requires careful ablation
Novelty claims are conditional on reaching specified accuracy thresholds — if MRF-DW < 0.15% improvement, the claim is falsified per the lifecycle contract

blocking_gaps.description: No actual training results exist — cannot verify that V2-E beats any baseline. All accuracy claims are extrapolated.
blocking_gaps.recommended_action: Train V2-E (tiny variant) on ImageNet-1K for 300 epochs with supervised learning protocol.

blocking_gaps.recommended_action: Implement FCMAE pretraining pipeline with sparse conv decoder and mask ratio 0.6.
